title: From Admission to Retention: Predicting Durable Offspring in Quality-Diversity Search
abstract: arXiv:2611.06522v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Automated failure discovery can be framed as a diversity problem: the objective is to expose distinct ways a system fails rather than a single critical adversarial case. Yet uniform parent sampling provides no way to allocate search effort toward individuals likely to produce durable archive contributions. We study this credit assignment problem in an unstructured Quality-Diversity (QD) archive, testing whether signals available before an individual has reproduced distinguish offspring that merely enter the archive from those still retained generations later. Across a planar-arm benchmark and two robotic-locomotion tasks, the same signals are often associated with entry and persistence in opposite directions. In particular, lineage depth is the clearest such signal, and its persistence discrimination grows with population capacity, which is associated with lower turnover. translated_title: 从准入到留存：在质量多样性搜索中预测持久留存的子代个体
translated_abstract: 自动化失效发现可以被构建为一个多样性问题：其目标是揭示系统失效的多种不同方式，而非单一的临界对抗样本。然而，均匀的父代采样无法将搜索精力分配给那些可能对档案产生持久贡献的个体。我们在一个非结构化的质量多样性档案中研究了这一信用分配问题，检验在个体繁殖之前可获得的信号能否区分那些仅仅进入档案的子代与那些在数代之后仍被保留的子代。在一个平面机械臂基准任务和两个机器人运动任务中，相同的信号往往以相反的方向与准入和留存相关联。特别地，谱系深度是最清晰的此类信号，且其留存区分能力随种群容量的增大而增强，这与更低的档案更替率相关联。
tldr: 该论文研究了质量多样性搜索中的信用分配问题，发现繁殖前可获得的信号（尤其是谱系深度）能够预测子代个体是仅短暂进入档案还是在多代之后仍被持久保留，且同一信号对准入与留存的影响方向往往相反。
en_tdlr: This paper studies credit assignment in unstructured Quality-Diversity archives, showing that pre-reproduction signals—most notably lineage depth—can predict whether offspring merely enter the archive or remain retained generations later, with the same signals often affecting admission and persistence in opposite directions.
